observed.claim: preflightDreamCycle in budget-code registers a bounded cycle and queries rolling spend, returning allow/refuse with remaining budget. It does not currently inspect pack provenance or scan status.

packerFacade in pack-code enforces pinned repomix identity, rejects empty include sets, and verifies the security scan completes before returning an artifact with engine provenance. Scan cannot be disabled.
pack-tests confirm that --no-security-check is absent from all constructed repomix arguments, and flag smuggling is refused outright.

candidate.hypothesis: Composing cost admission (A) with scanned-pack provenance (B) creates a single attestable boundary: a Dream cycle is only admitted if its extracted source evidence was scanned by the pinned engine and the scan passed. The pack artifact hash and scan attestation become part of the admission record, enabling offline verification that the code analyzed by the model was not substituted or unscanned. This closes the gap where admission could succeed but pack evidence could be missing, unscanned, or swapped.

A.uniqueContribution: Enforces cost ceiling via shared governor and rolling workspace spend, rejecting cycles that exceed per-cycle or 24-hour budgets. Provides the admission verdict and remaining budget context.
A.removalEffect: Without cost admission, there is no cost-based guard preventing unlimited Dream cycles, and no per-cycle or rolling-window budget enforcement. Operators lose budget visibility and ceiling enforcement.

B.uniqueContribution: Enforces that source evidence is explicitly scoped, produced by a pinned scanner with mandatory security scanning enabled, and returns signed provenance (engine identity, artifact hash, scan status). Refuses any attempt to disable or smuggle flags.
B.removalEffect: Without scanned-pack enforcement, source evidence can be unscanned, produce no audit trail, or be substituted. The pack mechanism has no guarantee that the code fed to the model was security-scanned or traced to a known engine.

relations.mapping: preflightDreamCycle accepts a cycle only if it will consume source evidence from packerFacade. The admission record stores the pack artifact hash and scan attestation returned by B. Refusal in either gate (cost or scan) prevents the cycle from starting.
preconditions: The Dream cycle must declare which source scopes (repository paths) it will analyze; these are passed to packerFacade as the include set.
packerFacade must complete its scan before preflightDreamCycle records the cycle as admitted.
Both A and B must agree on a shared attestation schema (pack hash, scan verdict, engine identity, timestamp).
transferRisks: If preflightDreamCycle admits a cycle but packerFacade later fails to produce a scanned pack, the admission is orphaned; the record must mark such cycles as incomplete or rolled back.
The pinned repomix identity used by B may diverge from the identity expected by A; version skew must be detected and rejected.
Cost estimates in A are based on cycle configuration, not actual pack size; a pack that consumes more tokens than estimated will exceed the rolling budget after admission.

assumptions: Both A and B assume the shared governor and rolling-window database queries (deps.check, deps.sumSince) are accurate and not subject to clock skew or concurrent mutation.
B assumes that the pinned repomix executable and its scanner are correctly installed and will not be replaced without triggering a verified identity check.
The composition assumes that a single Dream cycle uses exactly one scanned-pack artifact; multiplexing across packs or reusing old packs is out of scope.
Both units assume that the admission decision (allow/refuse) is final for the cycle; retries or deferred admission are not modeled.

knownRelatedWork.ref: Cost-gated API admission is standard in multi-tenant SaaS (e.g., OpenAI API tier gates, cloud billing limits). Rolling-window spend caps are common.
knownRelatedWork.overlap: A implements a known pattern; the novelty, if any, is in the specific rolling-window formula and the Dream-specific cycle registration.

knownRelatedWork.ref: Source scanning and provenance pinning are used in supply-chain integrity (SLSA, in-toto). Mandatory scanner invocation with no bypass is a known hardening technique.
knownRelatedWork.overlap: B implements standard scanner integration; the novelty, if any, is in the pinned identity enforcement and the refusal of flag-based disablement.

priorArt.proposedDelta: The proposed composition is distinct: cost admission (A) that is contingent on verified source provenance (B), such that a Dream cycle is only admitted if its code evidence was scanned. This closes a gap where an operator could admit a high-cost cycle without auditing what code was passed to the model. The composition requires A and B to share an attestation record and for B's scan verdict to be a precondition for A's allow decision.

experiment.baseline: Current behavior: preflightDreamCycle returns allow/refuse based only on cost gates. A scanned pack is prepared separately and may be stale, missing, or unscanned, with no dependency from admission to pack verification.
experiment.change: Modify preflightDreamCycle to accept an optional pack result from packerFacade (or a pack-scan attestation). If the pack scan failed or is absent, return allow=false with reason 'pack-scan-required-or-failed'. Store the pack artifact hash and scan timestamp in the admission record.
experiment.measurement: Observable: preflightDreamCycle rejects a Dream cycle request if packerFacade returns scan failure; accepts only if scan passed and hash is stored. Audit log shows pack hash and scan result alongside cost verdict.
experiment.successCriterion: A test case that calls preflightDreamCycle with a mock packerFacade returning a failed scan, and verifies that preflightDreamCycle returns allow=false with a pack-scan-related reason. A second test confirms allow=true only when both cost and scan gates pass, and both attestations are in the record.
experiment.falsifier: preflightDreamCycle returns allow=true even when packerFacade returns a failed-scan result, or the admission record does not include the pack scan attestation.

candidate.beneficiary: Capability packet reviewers and capability system operators who need confidence that evidence supporting contract claims remains valid across source changes and that conflicting contract revisions are detected deterministically before acceptance.
candidate.behavior: When a capability packet is submitted for review, the system verifies that all cited source excerpts match current disk state by hash, and when a behavioral contract is appended to a capability unit, the system refuses writes against stale expected revisions, returning a structured conflict that includes the actual revision number. Together, these prevent silent invalidation of evidence and deterministic acceptance of conflicting contract states.

observed.claim: Source-freshness capability performs byte-level hash validation of cited excerpts and full source files, invalidating packets when source edits, renames or deletions occur, and checks packet/excerpt size budgets before admitting cached evidence.

Spec-revisions capability uses row-locked compare-and-swap transactions in Postgres to serialize concurrent revision writes and refuse stale expected-revision inputs with a structured conflict response; real-database tests verify one-winner semantics and immutable history.

candidate.hypothesis: Composing source-freshness validation with spec-revision conflict detection creates a two-layer safety property: evidence supporting a capability contract must remain byte-identical to cited source (freshness-A), and any later revision of that contract must undergo deterministic conflict detection to prevent silent overwrite of prior accepted behavior (revisions-B). This composition reduces the risk that capability evidence becomes stale between acceptance and review, and that competing contract revisions silently overwrite each other. The transfer of freshness guarantees into the revision transaction requires that the packet's evidence identity be part of the expected-revision comparison, so that a source change in evidence automatically invalidates the prior contract as stale.

A.uniqueContribution: Byte-level source freshness validation: verifies that cited source excerpts and full files have not been edited, renamed or deleted since packet creation. Detects working-tree changes even without commit changes.
A.removalEffect: Without source-freshness, stale evidence supporting capability contracts could be accepted without detecting that the underlying implementation or test has changed, invalidating the contract claim.

B.uniqueContribution: Deterministic concurrent revision write serialization: uses row-locked compare-and-swap to refuse writes against stale expected revisions and return a structured conflict with actual revision, ensuring only one concurrent writer succeeds and prior revisions remain addressable.
B.removalEffect: Without spec-revisions, concurrent edits to a capability contract could overwrite each other silently, or stale revisions could be re-applied after newer ones are accepted, breaking contract history and making it impossible to audit which revision was actually in force.

relations.mapping: When a capability contract is revised via spec-revisions, the new revision must include the packet's source-freshness evidence as a subordinate identity. If source-freshness detects that cited evidence is stale, that stale-evidence identity should be included in the expectedRevision comparison in spec-revisions, so that a source change automatically causes any pending revision write to fail with a conflict, forcing re-evaluation of the contract claim against current source.
preconditions: The capability packet identity (including source hashes and excerpt identities) must be explicitly versioned in the spec-revision input so that source changes invalidate the prior contract assumption.

The spec-revision transaction must occur after source-freshness validation passes, or must re-validate freshness within the transaction lock to prevent TOCTOU races between freshness check and revision write.
transferRisks: If the spec-revision mechanism does not include the source-freshness evidence identity in its expectedRevision comparison, a source change would not prevent a stale contract revision from being written, re-introducing the silent-overwrite risk.

If freshness validation is not re-checked atomically within the revision transaction, a source change between freshness validation and revision write could allow a stale-evidence contract to be recorded without detection.
Postgres row locking guarantees only serialization; ownership and authorization checks are outside this evidence excerpt and must be verified separately.

assumptions: Source files are accessed via the same root path and readArtifact mechanism in both freshness and revision contexts, so hash validation is consistent.
The expectedRevision field in spec-revisions is intended to be a monotonically advancing integer, and source-freshness evidence identity can be mapped into that field without lossy representation.
Concurrent writes to spec-revisions use the same Postgres row-lock mechanism, and no out-of-band mutation of revisions occurs outside the setSpecClause transaction.
missingEvidence: Integration test or acceptance test showing freshness validation being called before or within a spec-revision write.
Explicit mapping of the capability packet identity and source hashes into the expectedRevision field or an adjacent immutable identity field in the spec-revisions contract.

Evidence that the CapabilityPacketSchema and SpecClauseInput schemas share a common versioning or identity namespace so that a source change in A invalidates B without requiring manual re-registration.

priorArt.proposedDelta: Embed the source-freshness evidence identity (source hashes and excerpt hashes) as an immutable part of the spec-revision identity, so that source-freshness validation failure automatically maps to a stale-expectedRevision conflict in the revision transaction. This prevents a contract from being recorded as accepted if its supporting evidence becomes invalid between freshness check and revision write, and ensures that source changes force re-evaluation of the contract claim.

experiment.baseline: A capability packet with evidence from implementation and tests is accepted. A source file referenced in that packet is edited. A new spec-revision is written with the same expectedRevision as before. Outcome: the revision write succeeds (current behavior, no integrated freshness check).
experiment.change: Add a freshness-revalidation step within the spec-revision transaction lock, which calls verifyCapabilityPacket on the packet before allowing the CAS write. If freshness returns false, the transaction returns a conflict instead of revising.
experiment.measurement: After source edit, attempt the same spec-revision write. Measure whether the transaction returns a conflict (new behavior) or succeeds (baseline).
experiment.successCriterion: The revision write fails with a conflict response (status: 'conflict' or a new 'evidence_stale' status) when source freshness is invalid, and succeeds only when all source evidence remains byte-identical.
experiment.falsifier: The revision write succeeds after source edit, or the system raises an uncaught error instead of returning a structured conflict response.
